**Visual analysis:**

- **Plant**: Tomato (*Solanum lycopersicum*), multiple compound leaves visible
- **Affected parts**: Leaves (upper surface clearly shown)
- **Key features**:
  - Numerous pale yellow to yellow-green irregular spots/patches scattered across the leaf surface
  - Interveinal chlorosis with a mottled appearance
  - Lesions lack the concentric rings of Early Blight or the water-soaked margins of Late Blight
  - Lower/older leaves appear more severely affected (greater yellowing)
  - No obvious dark sporulation masses visible on upper surface; spots are diffuse and irregular, not sharply defined circular lesions

**Reasoning through differentials:**

- **Early Blight**: Ruled out — no concentric target-ring lesions, no dark brown necrotic centers
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Ruled out — Septoria has well-defined circular spots with gray-white centers and dark borders; the spots here are more diffuse and yellowed
- **Bacterial Speck**: Ruled out — Bacterial Speck lesions are tiny (1–2 mm), dark brown-black with sharp halos; not matching the pale, larger irregular patches
- **Late Blight**: Ruled out — no water-soaked greasy lesions or white sporulation on undersides
- **Leaf Mold** (Fulvia fulva): **Best match** — characteristic pale green to yellow, irregular diffuse spots on the upper leaf surface of tomato; interveinal yellowing and chlorotic mottling are hallmarks; older/lower leaves affected first; spots correspond to fungal colonies visible from the underside
